3eecu:286: The technical value of MTP lies in solving the fundamental "memory bandwidth bottleneck" in LLM inference. Standard autoregressive generation produces only one token per step, yet each step requires moving billions of parameters — a contradiction that is especially pronounced on consumer GPUs and Apple Silicon. MTP's cleverness is that it does not try to make the large model generate one token faster (which is limited by hardware physics), but instead leverages the paradigm of "small model predicts multiple tokens, large model verifies in batch," batching the large model's computation so that the same memory bandwidth work yields more tokens. This approach — "no model architecture changes, no output quality degradation" — makes MTP one of the very few inference optimization solutions that delivers both engineering feasibility and guaranteed quality.

eakaoh:313: The MTP drafters' adaptation to Apple Silicon reveals the distinctive behavior patterns of MoE (Mixture of Experts) models on consumer hardware. The 26B MoE model shows limited acceleration at batch=1, because the expert routing mechanism cannot exploit its conditional computation advantage under low concurrency — most experts remain idle during single-request execution. When the batch size increases to 4-8, expert routing across multiple requests can overlap, and the drafter's multi-token prediction can better leverage parallelism, bringing the 2.2x speedup to light. This observation offers direct engineering guidance for developers deploying Gemma 4 on Apple Silicon: if you run only a single concurrent request, you may not perceive any speedup — you should use batching or concurrent requests to fully utilize the hardware.

xba6l6:333: KV Cache sharing is the most impactful engineering decision in the MTP architecture. In traditional speculative decoding, the drafter model and the target model each maintain independent KV caches; every draft token generated by the drafter requires recomputing the context activations already processed by the target model, incurring additional memory and compute overhead. Google's MTP has the drafter directly reuse the target model's KV cache and activations, essentially grounding the drafter's "predictions" on context representations already preprocessed by the large model. This not only eliminates redundant computation, but more importantly aligns the drafter's prediction space with the large model's representation space, significantly improving the batch acceptance rate — if the draft token representation space diverges from the target model's, mass rejections during verification would cancel out the acceleration gains.
